nodes.text: made a bargain with Thorgeir the lawspeaker that he should
proclaim it, though he was still a heathen then. And after men
came to their booths, Thorgeir lay down, and
spread his cloak over himself and rested all that day
and the night after, and did not speak a word. And in the morning
after, he sat up and sent word that men
should go to the Law Rock. And then he began
his speech, when men had come there, and said that it seemed to him
that men's affairs would then have come to a hopeless pass if men were
not all to have one law here in the land; and he put it to
men in many ways that they should not let that happen,
and said that it would lead to such discord that it could surely be
expected that such fighting would arise among men
as would lay the land waste. He told how
kings from Norway and from Denmark had kept up
war and battles between them for a long time, until
the people of the lands made peace between them, though they did not want it.
And that course worked out so that within a short time they were sending each other
treasures, and that peace held as long as they
lived. “And now it seems advisable to me,” he said, “that we
also do not let those prevail who most wish to oppose each other,
and that we so settle matters between them that each side
has something of its case, and that we all have one
law and one faith. It will prove true that if we tear
the law apart, we will tear apart the peace too.” And
he ended his speech in such a way that both sides agreed
that all should have the one law which he would decide to
proclaim. Then it was laid down in law that all men
should be Christian and receive baptism, those who before
were unbaptised here in the land; but on the exposure of infants
the old laws should stand, and on the eating of horse-meat.
People might sacrifice in secret if they wished, but it would carry
*fjǫrbaugsgarðr* [lesser outlawry] if witnesses came forward. But
